newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr must hold key levels to rise next week.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr must hold key levels to rise next week.

text.p: The dollar needs to hold above 1.71 marks and 125.00/15 yen through Friday and the weekend to start next week on strong footing, technical analysts said.

However, likely dollar volatility ahead of this weekend's meeting of Group of Seven finance ministers and summit talks between President Bill Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Friday could push the dollar below these key supports.
The greenback violated support overnight at 125.80 yen and remains on the defensive, analysts said.
"There are some studies like slow stochastics and parabolics that are in sell mode. There is the potential to see slippage to 125.40 yen," said John Moore, foreign exchange analyst at Technical Data.

"If anything, this pullback might give us better levels to buy the dollar. For now, you've got to respect the dollar move, but once we hear some statements from Clinton and Hashimoto and the G7, things will settle down and people will want to buy the dollar again," Moore added.
Analysts said the 125.30/50 yen area represents a "decent" buying opportunity, bar any unexpected G7 outcome.

"The important level with respect to the short-term bullish outlook is 125.03/15 (yen), which I don't think is going to be tested today," said Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at MMS International.
"Anywhere below 125.50 to 125.30 is a decent buy."
One hour before the U.S. midday, the dollar broke through resistance at 1.7210 marks, setting market sights on the 1.73 mark figure, with intermediate resistance at 1.7240/50.
The 1.7210 barrier capped a probe higher on Thursday and was also the March 6 high, analysts said.
The move boosted dollar/yen above the 126 threshold, but below resistance at 126.40.

Sparking the greenback's push higher was a wire service report which quoted Deutsche Bank chief economist Norbert Walter as saying the Group of Three would tolerate the dollar moving up to 1.80 marks and 130 yen.
The dollar rose to 1.7225/35 marks at 1100 EDT/1500 GMT from 1.7160/65 at the open and 125.95/05 yen from 125.62/67.
